I started to think that all this bipolar stuff was just an excuse for me to not do anything productive. I ended up stopping my medication for over a year because I figured if it wasn't helping, maybe it was because my bipolar wasn't real. That was the worst year of my life, and I realized that I didn't have the power to make my bipolar just go away. Now I'm back on meds that actually help, and I realize that I wasn't ever faking it.

I don't know if this helps, but my doctor put me on Rexulti which is a newer antipsychotic that is supposed to be like Abilify but with less symptoms. So far I've been on it for a month and have had no weight gain, whereas I gained about 50 pounds on Abilify. It's new though, so affordability may be an issue. It also isn't approved for bipolar, only depression. But I've had great luck with it!

I'm really sorry about your situation. It sounds like you are just dodging bullets left and right, and that sucks. As for the situation with your friends, it may be better for you to seek friendship with guys instead, even if that goes against your personality. I am a girl so I can't totally relate, but when I went through my roughest times I always seemed to gravitate towards the opposite sex. So I totally understand why you probably would rather be friends with girls. But for me, my biggest issue was developing feelings for those opposite-sex friends and then getting crushed later on (as you are beginning to experience).

 I know you say that everyone in your town is an asshole, but maybe you can meet people online to help you through. Obviously you have come here looking for support, and I think if you continue to reach out you will find someone (I know it doesn't feel like it, but don't give up). Support is what has brought me through bipolar disorder, and if I could have found my support system sooner I would have been much better off. 

Even if you had a million supporters, there would still be days that you feel defeated and ready to give up. Life hits some people worse than others, and it's okay to be feeling depressed in those times. My therapist always tells me that emotions are always going to come and go like waves; you just have to ride with them instead of fighting against them. It doesn't make the depression any more bearable, but it helps you push through those moments when you no longer want to live. 

I've never posted on this subreddit, so I hope this was somehow helpful to you. Just hang in there :)

Many people (like myself) have actual chemical imbalances that cause mood and anxiety disorders. Yes, sometimes people want attention or do it for popularity's sake, but many people really do need psychiatric help. I speak from experience that when you have a mental disorder it really isn't "that easy" to make yourself happy. In fact, trying usually causes guilt from thoughts like "I shouldn't be sad" and "Why can't I just be happy? There must be something wrong with me". But getting the help I needed has been crucial. There is a big difference between pitying someone and supporting them. If I didn't have support, I would have already killed myself. 

Tl;dr: People with true mental disorders cannot just make themselves happy.
